It’s not that flat oil benchmark prices crashed, perhaps more importantly the physical market sent an even stronger signal of the wave of supply. 

The physical premium in the Middle East market (Oman vs Dubai) plunged today to almost zero (from >$30 a barrel in mid Sept). In the Dated Brent market, the physical premium for North Sea crude plunged to minus ~$1 a barrel (it was plus ~$19 in early Oct). 

The physical premia in both the Middle East and North Sea markets is now the lowest in about 3 ½ months.

OIL FUNDS wait on sidelines for diplomacy or war

Investors made few changes to petroleum positions for the second week running despite bellicose rhetoric from the United States and Iran and a growing volume of commentary predicting an imminent resumption of hostilities.

Hedge funds and other money managers sold the equivalent of 15 million barrels in the six most important petroleum futures and options contracts over the seven days ending on October 27.

There has not been any significant change in the combined position since the middle of October and arguably since the end of September despite increasingly confident forecasts fighting will resume soon ...

On Friday Western Canadian Select (WCS) differentials in Hardisty, Alberta closed at $31.10/bbl under WTI, their widest diff since the all-time largest blowout in WCS diffs in 2018.

That 2018 blowout prompted provincial production curtailment, but that wouldn't help nearly as much this time—pain is on the far end of the pipeline.

Lots of people love to ask why the oil market could be "so gullible" as to sell off on every deal headline.

The challenge remains that while any one diplomatic headline hope is very unlikely to amount to much, the market's base case remains that this will end via some kind of deal.

So while this likely isn't the end, this is what the end will likely look like and you gotta kinda act accordingly so you don't get run over as this latest episode runs its course. 

Stay alive (and keep your job) to buy back on the other side if this once again isn't the one.

Imho this crude pullback is less about the market buying the promise of the flurry of diplomatic headlines and more that said headlines/change in tone reduces the probability that we're about to dive headlong back into re-escalation again immediately following the midterms.

El Niño strengthens, raising weather-related risks for global agriculture

El Niño continues to gather strength, with sea surface temperature anomalies in the central-eastern equatorial Pacific now exceeding the peak recorded during the powerful 2015–16 event. According to the latest weekly Niño 3.4 readings shown in the chart, temperatures have risen to approximately 3.4°C above the long-term average, well above the +0.5°C threshold commonly used to identify El Niño conditions. With the seasonal peak not expected until late November or early December, the event could strengthen further.

The rapid intensification raises the prospect of significant weather disruptions across major agricultural producing regions. Historically, strong El Niño events have been associated with hotter and drier conditions in Australia and parts of Southeast Asia, potentially affecting wheat, sugar, palm oil and rice production. Meanwhile, parts of South America may experience above-average rainfall, benefiting some crops while increasing the risk of flooding and harvest disruptions. Elsewhere, it is also worth noting a major short position held by speculators in the US gas futures market in anticipation of a milder winter and lower heating demand.

For commodity markets, the key issue is not simply the strength of the Pacific warming but how it translates into rainfall patterns, temperatures and growing conditions. The impact will vary considerably between regions and crops, with the potential for both supply losses and improved yields.

Commodities:

#CrudeOil: Brent tumbled 8% on Monday after Iran's leadership authorised further talks with Washington, with both presidents citing progress in Qatar-mediated negotiations despite significant differences remaining. Prices rebounded modestly today after US forces reportedly carried out limited defensive strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island following claims by the IRGC that it had downed US drones near the Strait of Hormuz. However, President Trump apparently ruled out resuming strikes after the midterms. The oil slump also weighed on other energy markets, with European gas futures falling almost 9% and US heating oil posting its steepest decline in six months.

Precious metals: #Gold rebounded strongly from Friday's slump as tumbling oil prices initially improved risk sentiment. However, gold encountered renewed selling near USD 3,970, a former support level now acting as resistance. The rejection highlights fragile sentiment, with technical and momentum-driven selling continuing to outweigh longer-term investor demand. Attention now turns to today's US midterms, global equities, Middle East developments, and energy prices.

#Copper's recent resilience is being tested, with prices falling 2.8% in Asian trading to USD 6.38, challenging recent lows in the USD 6.30–6.40 area. Despite supportive structural fundamentals, the short-term path of least resistance appears lower amid broader metals weakness, renewed equity market selling and growing questions over the AI and data centre demand narrative. Adding to the pressure, the yuan weakened after the PBOC moved to curb its recent appreciation, making dollar-denominated copper more expensive for Chinese buyers. For now, these headwinds are overshadowing tight physical markets and constrained mine supply.

Are the hunters about to become the hunted?

Precious metals continue to stage a strong recovery, gaining further momentum over the past couple of hours as crude oil prices slump on renewed hopes for a negotiated end to the Middle East conflict. The latest optimism follows reports that Iran's supreme leader has authorised the government to pursue talks aimed at resolving the months-long conflict.

As highlighted in my #gold update earlier today, Friday's break below key support at USD 3,970 triggered an acceleration in technical and momentum-driven short selling, compounded by further long liquidation.

However, with sentiment improving and gold rebounding, the focus is now shifting towards the risk of a short squeeze. For sellers to come under meaningful pressure, gold must first reclaim the former support level at USD 3,970, now turned resistance. A sustained move back above USD 4,000 would provide a stronger signal that downside momentum is fading, potentially forcing recently established shorts to cover.

The sharp decline in crude oil prices is also helping ease inflation concerns and the associated pressure on bond yields, providing an additional tailwind for precious metals. However, much will depend on whether diplomatic optimism translates into tangible progress and whether the broader recovery in risk sentiment can be sustained.

Whether gold can clear these technical hurdles remains to be seen. But after Friday's aggressive selling, the risk-reward balance for short sellers may be starting to shift. For now, at least, the hunters may be wondering whether they are about to become the hunted. #XAUUSD #silver #XAGUSD
